Finer dining in Hanoi
Feb 2025 • Couples
This restaurant has been recommended to us so e decided to try it after a day of sight seeing in Hanoi.
It’s situated in the Old Town and is in a good location
The restaurant has a small frontage onto the street, but once you go inside the place is much bigger. The restaurant also has more tables on the first floor, where you get a nice breeze when the balcony doors are open.
The food was really good. I had fried spring rolls to start, which were delicious. The day before we had eaten on the street, and whilst those were good, the Blue Butterflies were much finer, with a more delicate taste and presentation. Tasty dipping sauce too. I then had the “ Bo Loc Lac” ( stir fried beef) which was fabulous. The Beef was really tender and soft with a good element of spice to the dish.
My partner had duck breast to start and the stuffed chicken as a main followed by the coconut coffee. She really enjoyed them!!
Overall, this is a great restaurant that provides a bit more of a finer dining experience than most.

Great food and service at a reasonable price
Dec 2023 • Family
This restaurant is situated in the old quarter close to the famous beer corner, a junction away.
The road it is on is considered reasonably quiet in an otherwise bustling area of Hanoi. It is a two storey restaurant situated in quite a narrow shophouse of Hanoi. There are not many tables in the restaurant so it is advised to make a reservation. Most hotels will be able to do that for you.
The food in this restaurant is a mix of western and Vietnamese which the 4 of us ordered. Both types of food were found to be quite well prepared and delicious. The rosemary chicken was moist and not dry, the spring rolls were fresh and the pumpkin soup was more savoury than sweet. The 4 cocktails and mocktails we ordered were quite ingeniously prepared and original to the restaurant.
The service in this restaurant also deserves mention. The ratio of staff to patrons is high and the staff are very attentive to details such as a misplaced servette, water than needs to be topped up and so on even though they do not wait at your table. It was never difficult to get the attention of any of the staff when needed.
And finally price. We ordered 4 full dishes, 3 sides, 4 cocktails/mocktails and it all came up to 1,900,000 dong which is very reasonable in Hanoi.
In conclusion the 4 of us had a wonderful experience in this establishment without burning a hole in our wallet.

Friendly and very helpful staff who have a good grip of English, a bi-lingual menu that has accurate photos of all the dishes on offer, good variety of drinks, impeccable service. A stand-out in an area chock-full of eateries. The option of small flask bottles of 5 or 6 local ruou rice wines. An egg coffee that could pass as a light dessert : all within a traditional Hanoi 'tube-house'...and thoughtful, inviting decor : the little touches too, like cinnamon bark used as a chopstick 'rest'. There's a lot of thought gone into this place.
When you go upstairs to the toilet you'll more than likely pass a cookery class going on !
My advice ? Order the first thing on the menu - 5 local specialities including banh xeo pancake, spring rolls Hanoi-style, and a sticky black-rice pudding you could eat a bucket of !
If you're in Hanoi, hungry and eager to try great local food...stop reading and go !
